attributes.calibration: The new test_r66_cv_probe suite covers wrong baselines on all eight axes before variant launch, successful fidelity, unknown axes/jobs/functions, empty parses, failed requested variants, duplicate outputs, insensitive controls, zero-exit ignored-option diagnostics, missing executables/compilers, cleanup failure, stale-output refusal and both Ninja path forms. test_r64_postprocess_audit now asserts the repaired synthetic refusal rather than merely characterizing the old bug.
implementation: Every axis checks whole-object fidelity; baseline is compiled once, then reused. Unknown axes/jobs/functions and empty object parses refuse explicitly. Failed or missing compiler/runner, missing output, and failed extab cleanup cannot become negative matching results. Old output is removed before an attempted replacement so stale bytes cannot mask failure.

JSON records the Ninja edge/template, ordered flags and executed argv/stdout/stderr/return codes, compiler/object/source/build-graph hashes, finite requested/completed matrix, duplicate object outputs, per-function normalized-assembly hashes, sensitive sibling controls and lexical pragma ranges. The lexical inventory expressly does not evaluate includes, conditionals, push/pop or effective compiler option precedence.

read_edges accepts forward- and backslash Ninja paths; compile commands retain the actual generated wibo/wine runner prefix. An unsupported or unresolved runner/template refuses. Cross-platform parsing/runner reconstruction is fixture-tested; a Linux live compiler run was not performed in this Windows lane.

The raw boundary is the Ninja compile edge and includes extab cleanup when that edge uses it; it is not automatically pristine compiler output. Existing compile_with callers retain the five-argument (path, error) API.

subject: tool:composed-census-cv-probe
value: Compiler-sweep validity repair, not a new matching result or a compiler-necessity proof. cv_probe now stops every supported axis before variants if a fresh full-TU compile differs from the actual raw Ninja object. Its optional schema_version=1 JSON distinguishes completed finite experiments (PASS/0), rejected trial commands (FAIL/1), and unavailable inputs/fidelity or incomplete measurements (UNRESOLVED/2). Matchtool's OK/OK~ scores remain diagnostic and do not certify datum/relocation identity. No game source, production compiler selection, split, or postprocessor rule was changed.
